title: Compiling C and Reading Diagnostics

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: A C implementation translates source through preprocessing, compilation, assembly, and linking. Use a command such as `cc -std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic main.c -o main` so warnings expose suspicious conversions and unused values. The compiler checks syntax and types but cannot prove every memory access is valid. Linker errors usually indicate a declared function or object has no matching definition. Read the first relevant diagnostic, correct one cause, rebuild, and never run a stale executable after compilation fails.
keyPoints: A C implementation translates source through preprocessing, compilation, assembly, and linking.
commonMistakes: macros do textual substitution without type checking
ignoring warnings can leave real defects
